class.noble.EUR: a family of barons and counts
class.slave.family.EUR: into a family of serfs bound to their lord's land
class.peasant.family.EUR: into a family of free peasants
prof.farmer.as.EUR: a peasant on your own holding
prof.farmer.desc.EUR: Your own strips of land, dues to the lord, a tithe to the Church and the constant fear of a bad harvest.
prof.laborer.desc.EUR: Harvests, building sites, hauling loads - for a few coins a day.
prof.artisan.as.EUR: a journeyman in a guild workshop
prof.artisan.desc.EUR: You work for a guild master: boots, pots, horseshoes. The guild watches quality and prices.
prof.weaver.desc.EUR: Distaff and loom: wool and linen for the household and for sale.
prof.merchant.desc.EUR: Fairs, tolls at every bridge and long roads. You can grow rich - or go bankrupt.
prof.sailor.desc.EUR: Barges on the river, cogs at sea: wine, wool, herring. Dangerous, but the pay is decent.
prof.soldier.desc.EUR: A spearman, archer or mercenary in a lord's company. Plunder, wounds and long campaigns.
prof.scribe.desc.EUR: You draw up contracts, wills and charters in Latin. Few can write, so you are valued.
prof.physician.desc.EUR: You heal by Galen and Avicenna: urine, pulse, bloodletting. Honourable and well paid.
prof.priest.desc.EUR: You say Mass, baptise, marry and bury. You live on the tithe and know every sin in the parish.
prof.landholder.desc.EUR: Your own estate and village: rents, labour services, the manor court and your duty to your liege.
prof.magistrate.desc.EUR: You judge and collect taxes in the name of the king or the city. Power, expenses and dangerous enemies.
prof.matron.desc.EUR: The keys to the stores, the servants, the accounts - and the defence, when the lord is away at war.
prof.household_slave.as.EUR: a household serf at the lord's manor
prof.household_slave.desc.EUR: The lord's kitchen, stables and bakehouse. You cannot leave: you belong to the land.
prof.field_slave.desc.EUR: Three days a week on the lord's fields, the rest on your own patch of land.
prof.officer.desc.EUR: You lead a company of men-at-arms, pay them and answer for every one.
prof.workshop_owner.desc.EUR: Your own workshop, journeymen, apprentices and a voice in the guild.
prof.shipowner.desc.EUR: Your own cogs and barges, your own share in every voyage.
prof.official.desc.EUR: Service in the chancery: writs, seals, the accounts of the exchequer.
prof.overseer.desc.EUR: A serf chosen by the village and approved by the lord: you oversee labour services and answer for arrears.
prof.monk.desc.EUR: Eight services a day, the Rule of Saint Benedict, the scriptorium and the cloister garden. The world stays outside the wall.
prof.wool_merchant.desc: English fleece, Flemish and Florentine cloth. Wool is the gold of Europe.
prof.banker.desc: A money-changer's bench, bills of exchange, branches in Bruges and London. The Church condemns usury, and kings ask for loans.
prof.cathedral_mason.as: a mason on the cathedral works
prof.cathedral_mason.desc: You cut stone for a cathedral your grandchildren will finish. The scaffolding is high and falls are hard.
prof.alewife.desc: You brew ale and sell it to the neighbours. A bush hangs over your door, and the town's ale-taster comes to call.
prof.minstrel.desc: Songs of love and deeds in castles, at weddings and fairs. Today a feast, tomorrow the road.
prof.knight.desc: A horse, armour and an oath to your lord. Forty days of service a year, tournaments and wars.
lifestyle.food.plain.desc.EUR: Bread, pottage, peas, ale or wine
lifestyle.food.varied.desc.EUR: Meat, fish on fast days, cheese, wine
lifestyle.food.feasts.desc.EUR: Feasts with swans, spices and minstrels. Expensive
lifestyle.exercise.gymnasium.desc.EUR: Riding, falconry, sword practice. Stronger and healthier
lifestyle.medicine.temple.desc.EUR: Candles to the saints, vows, water from a holy well
lifestyle.medicine.physician.desc.EUR: A university physician reads urine and stars. Expensive
lifestyle.baths.daily.desc.EUR: Steam, hot tubs, gossip. You must live in a town
focus.learn.desc.EUR: A parish or cathedral school: the psalter, Latin, reckoning. The family has to pay
focus.study.desc.EUR: A master, books, Latin and disputations. It costs money
focus.service.desc.EUR: Arms practice and campaigns with your lord
ev.slave_assignment.text.EUR: The reeve decides what work you'll do on the lord's land. You could try asking for something you want.
ev.contubernium.title.EUR: A wedding by the lord's leave
ev.contubernium.text.EUR: A serf cannot marry without the lord's leave and a fee. But the steward lets you live with the one you love - someone from another village, and so from another lord's service.
ev.escape.text.EUR: They say whoever lives in a free town for a year and a day can never be reclaimed by his lord. Tonight an empty merchant's cart stands at the edge of the village.
ev.escape.flee.success.EUR: You reached the town and vanished among the day labourers. After a year and a day you are free.
ev.escape.flee.failure.EUR: The lord's men found you on the third day and brought you back to the land. The punishment was harsh.
prof.translator.desc.EUR: You turn Arabic books on stars, numbers and diseases into Castilian and Latin - together with scholars of three faiths.
